During hyperinflation, currency rapidly depreciates, leading to a sharp decline in purchasing power. To protect wealth in this environment, the following assets are usually considered relatively safe:

Precious Metals

Gold and silver have historically been viewed as hedges against inflation. Their intrinsic value is unaffected by specific monetary systems, and they often maintain or even increase their value during economic instability.

Real Assets

Real assets such as real estate, farmland, and forests can usually preserve value, and even appreciate during periods of hyperinflation. These assets not only have practical uses but can also generate rent or agricultural income.

Foreign Exchange

Holding relatively stable foreign currencies, such as the US Dollar, Swiss Franc, or other trusted international currencies, can hedge against the depreciation of the domestic currency.

Cryptocurrencies

In some cases, cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin are viewed as a tool against inflation because of their limited supply and lack of direct influence from government policies. However, the cryptocurrency market is highly volatile, requiring cautious investment.

Inflation-Protected Bonds

In some countries, government-issued inflation-protected bonds (such as TIPS in the US) are linked to the inflation index, providing protection.

Stocks

Stocks in certain industries, such as commodity producers, energy companies, and other businesses related to basic resources, may perform well during inflation because they can pass rising costs onto consumers.

Commodities

Commodities such as oil, natural gas, and grain often see price increases during inflation. Investing in these commodities can hedge against inflation risk.

Collectibles

Collectibles such as artworks, antiques, and luxury watches, which have intrinsic value and relatively independent markets, may maintain their value during hyperinflation.

item.title: A Reflection on the Historic Surge of A-Shares: False Prosperity or Steady Ascent?
item.description: The Largest Single Day Surge in the History of China's Stock Market
item.content:encoded:
The Shanghai Composite Index surged by 8.06% today, breaking the 3300 point barrier. Trading volume across both markets reached a massive 2.6 trillion yuan, setting a new historical high. All stock brokerage stocks hit the upper limit (limit up). Faced with such a fierce rally, many people cannot help but wonder: How long can this crazy surge last? Should we take profits now?

Personally, I believe that this market trend is unlikely to be a fleeting phenomenon; rather, it is a medium-term process that may last for two or three months.

What exactly happened in today’s market?

Today, the three major A-share indices opened and rose collectively. The Shanghai Composite Index closed up 8.06%, standing above 3300 points; the Shenzhen Component Index rose 10.67%; and the ChiNext Index rose 15.36%. Furthermore, the Beijing Stock Exchange 50 and the STAR 50 rose by 22.84% and 17.88% respectively, both setting new records for the largest single-day gains. The total trading volume reached 259.3 billion yuan, an increase of over 114.7 billion yuan compared to the previous trading day. Although there was a net outflow of 51.7 billion yuan in capital from the overall market, the market presented a broad-based rally—5,336 stocks rose, only 8 fell, 713 stocks hit the upper limit, and 2 stocks hit the lower limit.

The various faces in the market

Today, I observed the reactions of various participants. There is a significant polarization between market newcomers and veterans.

Many market veterans are still in a wait-and-see attitude. Few people have actually entered the market, and those who have entered hold relatively small positions. Their thinking is that this wave of ascent is unsustainable, and a massive crash could happen tomorrow. Therefore, their trading style is quick in and quick out—making a quick profit and leaving.

In contrast, new investors who are experiencing such a massive surge for the first time are generally optimistic, even blindly so. They lack risk awareness. Continuous profits make them overly confident, believing they can make a huge profit in the stock market and walk away unscathed.

Why is the market so frenzied?

First, it must be said that this is the largest single-day gain I have witnessed. Today, various online groups have been bustling with activity, with both bulls and bears being extremely active. People’s attention to the stock market has reached a new height. Since the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) announced its personal intervention to purchase financial assets on September 24th:

  • Capital Inflow: A large amount of capital, lacking investment targets, poured into the A-share market, directly driving up the market.
  • Short Covering: As the market rose at an extremely fast pace, a large number of short sellers who used margin financing were forced to cover their positions, further pushing the market higher.
  • New Blood: The market has gone 8 years without a period of prosperity, and a new generation of young people who have never experienced a stock market boom are now ready to enter.

How is this market rise different from before?

Unlike in the past, I believe this time’s rise has clear distinctions from previous ones:

  • PBOC’s Personal Intervention: This time, the PBOC is not merely guiding policy; it is personally purchasing financial assets and establishing two structural monetary policy tools: the swap facility for securities, funds, and insurance companies, as well as stock repurchases and increased lending for share purchases. This scale of capital injection is unprecedented.

  • Clear Policy Direction: This rise is not simply a “harvesting of韭菜” (cutting leeks/profiteering on retail investors); rather, it is aimed at driving the prosperity of financial assets, which in turn pushes sectors like real estate, thereby alleviating downward economic pressure. This goal clearly requires a medium-to-long-term market rise, not just short-term volatility.

What will the future trend be?

Due to the public holiday, the market will be closed for 7 days starting tomorrow. After the holiday, the market may first experience a wave of correction, as many people hope to realize their paper profits. This is human nature—people prefer certain returns and crave the security of having profits in hand.

However, they will find that after a short-term market correction, the market will advance further upward, which is determined by the goals of this round of stimulus. Those who exited the market after realizing profits will be distressed by the market’s continuous climb, feeling that they cut off their gains too early. Consequently, some people will re-enter the market, and they will do so with even larger amounts of capital (just as Newton, the founder of physics, did during the stock market bubble).

Next, the market will reach a state of artificial prosperity. However, this prosperity certainly cannot last indefinitely.

  • Firstly, the fundamental economic conditions have not improved, and personal incomes have not increased. Although those holding financial assets have gained returns, the economy of the vast majority of people remains far from optimistic.
  • Secondly, real estate is facing huge inventory pressure. With only 8 million newborns this year, real estate cannot truly gain support from demand.

Ultimately, the artificial prosperity built upon strong stimulus will gradually cool down.

Conclusion

Behind today’s massive surge in the A-share market, the PBOC’s direct intervention is undoubtedly the key driving factor, and the reactions of different groups in the market have further amplified the market volatility. Although this rise has brought significant market prosperity in the short term, from a macroeconomic and structural perspective, this prosperity carries great uncertainty. The market may experience a correction after the holiday, followed by continued upward movement driven by policy, potentially entering a state of artificial prosperity. However, the pressure from the fundamental economy and the real estate market will eventually cause the market heat to cool down.

On September 24, 2024, the Central Bank held a press conference and announced a new round of economic stimulus plan, which aims to inject approximately 300 billion yuan into the stock market, stating that further capital injections will continue in the future. This measure may attract a large influx of funds into the market in the short term, bringing about short-term prosperity. However, the sustainability of this effect remains questionable.

Motives Behind the Economic Stimulus

Why launch a new round of stimulus policy at this time? I believe the main reason is the continuous deterioration of the economic situation. It seems unlikely that the government can achieve the 5% GDP growth target this year, and this move appears to be a last-ditch effort.

As a large amount of capital enters the stock market, a wave of upward momentum is indeed possible. The overall capital volume in the current A-share market is not large, so this massive injection of funds can certainly push up the stock market in the short term. However, how long it can be sustained depends on the intensity of subsequent policies and the determination of the decision-makers.

Long-Term Economic Fundamentals Still Face Challenges

Although the stock market may rise in the short term, from a long-term perspective, the economic fundamentals have not fundamentally changed, and specific problems still exist:

  • Corporate profit margins are continuously declining
  • Unemployment rate has not shown significant improvement
  • The “only rising, never falling” myth of the real estate market has been shattered
  • Heavily indebted homeowners are not keen on taking on more leverage

From an economic perspective, when an economy faces a recession, interest rate cuts are usually seen as an effective means of stimulating market vitality and promoting economic growth. However, the effectiveness of interest rate cuts relies on businesses and individuals being willing to borrow at low interest rates and invest. When corporate profits are slim and individuals face the risk of unemployment, even if the cost of borrowing decreases, few people are willing to increase their debt—this is what is known as a “balance sheet recession.”

Shift in Consumption and Investment Expectations

Currently, signs of stagnation have appeared, mainly reflected in the change in people’s expectations for the future. Many people no longer expect promotions and salary increases; this change in expectation directly leads to a contraction in consumption and investment.

Real estate, as the core pillar of the Chinese economy, is unlikely to be re-driven by this round of stimulus. The reason is that market expectations have undergone a profound shift, and the bursting of the bubble has become a reality.

Changes in the Real Estate Market

In the past, people were willing to leverage their “six wallets” (meaning pooling money from multiple family members) to purchase homes, not merely because housing was a basic necessity. Besides basic living needs, almost nothing is an absolute necessity. At that time, housing possessed strong financial attributes, and people generally believed that housing prices would continue to rise, meaning investing in real estate could bring generous returns. Therefore, they viewed home buying not as a liability, but rather as a guaranteed profitable investment. Looking at historical data, the national average housing price rose from 500 yuan per square meter to 20,000 yuan, confirming that past investments yielded returns. However, the current market logic has fundamentally changed.

Conclusion

In summary, I believe the effect of this round of economic stimulus policy will be quite limited. The real estate market will remain sluggish, and after a brief frenzy, the stock market may quickly return to calm, with the index potentially falling below 3,000 points again. The long-term economic challenges still exist, and this stimulus is unlikely to fundamentally reverse the situation.

item.title: Producer Surplus and Consumer Surplus
item.description:
When discussing economics, Producer Surplus is an important concept. It refers to the difference between the actual income received by a producer or supplier when selling goods in the market at a certain price, and the minimum income they expected when willing to sell those goods at that price.

Simply put, Producer Surplus is the net gain of the producer in a transaction. Its calculation involves two key factors:

Producer’s Supply Price: This refers to the price at which the producer is willing to sell the goods or services. Typically, the producer’s supply price is related to their marginal cost (the extra cost of producing one unit of goods), because they hope to at least cover the production cost.

Simply put, Producer Surplus is the net gain of the producer in a transaction. Its calculation involves two key factors:

Producer’s Supply Price: This refers to the price at which the producer is willing to sell the goods or services. Typically, the producer’s supply price is related to their marginal cost (the extra cost of producing one unit of goods), because they hope to at least cover the production cost.

Market Price: This refers to the price the buyer is willing to pay, which is the market price of the goods or services.

The calculation formula for Producer Surplus is as follows:

Producer Surplus = Producer’s Supply Price - Market Price

Producer Surplus represents the net gain obtained by the producer when selling goods at a lower supply price. Producer Surplus occurs when the market price is higher than the producer’s supply price, because the producer sells the goods at a lower price but receives a higher actual income. If the market price is lower than the producer’s supply price, the Producer Surplus will be negative, meaning the producer may incur a loss in the transaction.

Producer Surplus is very important for understanding market operation and the supply-demand relationship. In a free market, the balance of supply and demand determines the market price, and Producer Surplus helps us understand the producer’s profitability at different price levels. When the market is in equilibrium, Producer Surplus is maximized, meaning the producer achieves maximum profit.

Okay, Consumer Surplus is an economic term that refers to the economic benefit or value obtained by consumers when purchasing goods or services. Its calculation method is:

Consumer Surplus = Consumer’s Reservation Price (Expected Price) - Actual Paid Price

For a simple example, assume the reservation price for an item is 100 Yuan for the consumer. If the actual market price is 80 Yuan, then the Consumer Surplus obtained by that consumer when purchasing the item is 100 - 80 = 20 Yuan.

Consumer Surplus reflects the net gain obtained by the consumer after purchasing goods or services. The larger the Consumer Surplus, the higher the economic utility obtained by the consumer. Increasing Consumer Surplus can usually raise total social welfare. The government employs many measures to increase Consumer Surplus, such as subsidies, tax incentives, etc.

In a free competitive market, when the wage level of a certain profession or industry is higher than the value deserved by the labor output or skills for that job, it attracts more people to study that profession and enter that market. As the supply increases, the number of workers in the market grows, which subsequently causes the wage level to decrease, eventually approaching the value deserved by the labor output.

This phenomenon is known in economics as the “Marginal Productivity Theory.” It posits that there is a relationship between the wage level and the marginal output of labor (which is the increase in output generated by adding one unit of labor). When a certain profession’s wage is higher than its marginal output, it attracts more people to join, thereby increasing the labor supply, which in turn lowers the wage level until the marginal output and the wage level reach equilibrium.

This phenomenon is common across many professions and industries. When supply and demand in the market tend towards equilibrium, the wage level usually tends towards the value of the marginal output—this is the situation you mentioned where profit approaches zero. In the long run, the market forms a relatively stable equilibrium state, and the wage level adjusts to match the skills, labor output, and market demand.

This also explains why continuous learning and skill improvement are extremely important for individuals to achieve success and obtain better compensation in the workplace. By constantly improving one’s skills and knowledge, an individual can maintain competitiveness in a fierce market and achieve better economic returns.

If you wish to earn extra profit beyond the value of the labor itself in the labor market, you can consider the following strategies:

Differentiation and Specialization: Find the field or specific skill you excel in, and continuously refine it to become an expert. Through differentiation and specialization, you can provide higher quality and more specialized services, thereby creating higher market value for yourself.

Creating Unique Value: Identify the pain points or needs in the market and provide unique solutions. Understand the customer’s true needs and offer services that exceed their expectations. This can win you more customers and positive word-of-mouth, leading to extra profit beyond the value of the labor itself.

Building a Personal Brand: Establish your visibility and authority in the industry through effective branding and personal promotion. A reputable and credible personal brand can bring you more business opportunities and chances, potentially leading to higher returns.

Mastering Composite Skills: Learning and mastering skills across multiple fields allows you to become a versatile individual. Possessing multiple skills increases your flexibility and adaptability, better meeting market demands, which brings you more opportunities and potential profits.

Innovation and Leadership: Continuously innovating and leading teams to achieve goals can bring you more business opportunities and project collaborations, thereby creating extra profit for you.

It is important to emphasize that pursuing extra profit beyond the value of the labor itself is not easy; it requires a significant investment of time, effort, and resources. Furthermore, success is not achieved overnight; it requires continuous effort and ongoing learning and growth. The key is to find the development path and strategy that suits you and continuously optimize and adjust it through practice. In a fiercely competitive market, only by continuously enhancing your value can you gain more opportunities and profits in the workplace.

Modern economics covers many important concepts and theories. Here are some of the main concepts:

Supply and Demand Theory: Supply and Demand Theory is one of the most fundamental concepts in economics, describing the relationship between supply and demand in the market for goods and services. It involves the formation and regulation mechanism of prices.

Marginal Analysis: Marginal Analysis emphasizes the importance of considering marginal changes in decision-making. Marginal cost, marginal utility, marginal productivity, etc., are core concepts of marginal analysis.

Opportunity Cost: Opportunity cost refers to the highest value of the alternative or opportunity that is given up when a certain action is chosen. It emphasizes the impact of considering opportunity cost on economic behavior.

Utility Theory: Utility Theory focuses on individual preferences and utility. It studies how individuals maximize utility when faced with choices, involving concepts such as diminishing marginal utility and utility functions.

Production Function: The production function describes the relationship between inputs and outputs, i.e., how input factors are converted into output. The production function is an important tool for studying production efficiency and output growth.

Cost Theory: Cost Theory studies the cost structure and decision-making process in a firm’s production. It includes concepts such as fixed costs, variable costs, marginal costs, etc., which are highly significant for a firm’s operational decisions.

Market Structure: Market structure studies the number, size, and interaction methods of different market participants. Common market structures include monopoly, oligopoly, competitive markets, etc.

Information Economics: Information Economics studies the transmission and utilization of information in the economy. It considers the impact of information incompleteness and asymmetry on market efficiency and resource allocation.

Externality: Externality refers to the non-market impact generated by the actions of an economic agent on others or society. Externality can be positive (positive externality) or negative (negative externality).

Public Goods: Public goods are items that cannot be excluded from individual use, and one person’s use does not affect others. Public goods usually require government intervention for provision and maintenance.

What? Are Money Values Tiered?

Does the money of the rich hold more value than the money of the ordinary person? Why is that? Is it because the rich spend money better than the ordinary person? Or is it because they possess some special investment strategy? In this article, we will explore the differences between the money of the rich and the ordinary, and provide some practical suggestions to help ordinary people achieve wealth growth.

The Money of the Rich Has Potential Growth Value

Let’s start with a simple example. Suppose both the rich and the ordinary person have 10,000 yuan. For the ordinary person, this 10,000 yuan might be used for daily expenses, such as clothes, pants, bags, rent, or mortgage payments. Although these expenses are necessary, they do not generate any additional income. In contrast, the rich person’s 10,000 yuan might be invested in stocks, bonds, real estate, etc. While these investments carry a certain risk, they can also bring substantial returns.

For example, suppose the rich person invests 10,000 yuan in a stock with an annualized return rate of 10%. Then, next year, this 10,000 yuan will become 11,000 yuan, and the year after, it will become 12,100 yuan, and so on. This potential growth value makes the rich person’s money more valuable than the ordinary person’s money.

The Rich Spend Money More Prudently

So, why are the rich more cautious when spending money? It is because they need to consider the potential consequences of spending, including the impact on future income. For the rich, spending 10,000 yuan is not just spending 10,000 yuan; it means giving up potential investment returns. Therefore, they consider the necessity and potential consequences of spending more carefully.

For instance, suppose the rich person needs to buy a new car. They might consider factors such as the car’s price, fuel efficiency, maintenance costs, and compare it with other investment opportunities. They might ask themselves:

  • Is this car worth spending so much money on?
  • Are there better investment opportunities?

This cautious attitude makes the rich more rational and prudent in their spending.

Spending Ratio of the Rich vs. Ordinary People

So, what is the difference in the spending ratio between the rich and the ordinary person? According to research, the income of the ordinary person is often entirely used for expenses, while the spending ratio of the rich is extremely low. For example, suppose the ordinary person’s monthly income is 5,000 yuan, and they might use their entire income for expenses, such as rent, mortgage, and living costs. In contrast, the rich person’s monthly income might be 50,000 yuan, but their spending ratio might only be 1%. This means they have more money available for investment and savings.

Conclusion

By exploring the differences between the money of the rich and the ordinary, we found that the rich person’s money is more valuable because it has potential growth value. We also found that the rich are more prudent when spending, because they need to consider the potential consequences of spending. Finally, we learned that there is a significant difference in the spending ratio between the rich and the ordinary.

Recommendations

So, how can ordinary people achieve wealth growth by changing their spending habits and investment strategies? Here are some practical suggestions:

  • Start Investing: Consider using your money for investment. How to invest is another serious topic.
  • Reduce Expenses: Try to reduce your spending ratio, leaving more money for investment and savings.
  • Spend Prudently: When spending, consider the potential consequences of the expenditure, including the impact on future income.

By taking these measures, ordinary people can begin to achieve wealth growth and make their money more valuable.
